title.value: Configure the redirect facility from the CLI

inlines.value: How your site’s URL redirects should be configured depends on the web server or service you use to serve your site.

If you use the default redirect facility, Antora will generate HTML pages that use the meta refresh feature of HTML to route the visitor to the target page (i.e., bounce page). When you inspect the output of your site, you will find pages that end with
tag inside a minimal HTML structure. If you have specified a start page for your site, this will include a
page at the root of your published site.
If you use any other redirect facility, Antora will not generate these bounce pages. (In other words, don’t expect to find the

page at the root of your published site). Instead, Antora relies on the web server to apply the redirect rules that it generates. For details about these rules and where they are written, see the sections below.

Redirect rules for start pages and page aliases are defined using the 301 HTTP status code, which means the redirect is considered permanent. Redirect rules for the latest version aliases are defined using the 302 HTTP status code, which means the redirect is considered temporary.

When a redirect configuration file is used, entries are sorted by component, version (reverse), module, then publication URL of the alias “from”. If a supplemental entry is added for the index.html path, that entry comes before the entry for the corresponding directory path.
The locations in the web server-specific redirect/rewrite rules match the URL of the pages as they are accessed in the site, and thus depend on the value of the
